mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings, lowering the present value of expected cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-trend window (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same or
failure_condition: 20-day out-of-sample backtest shows no significant positive return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day pre-trend average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, the central bank's higher policy rate reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not show significant negative excess returns relative to a 3% FEDFUNDS baseline (p > 0.05).
